rows.currentScript: Start at 'pop!' on line 14. Line 15 lands him 'in the warm grass of a great meadow'. So he comes up in the meadow. The carriage-drive is earlier, the hedge and river later.
rows.whyRewrite: 'The carriage-drive is earlier' treats it as a place the Mole passed. Line 10 only compares his tunnel to a carriage-drive owned by other animals, so this reinforces the literal reading the distractor is tagged for (en-figurative-taken-literally). Say the tunnel is only being compared to a carriage-drive.

rows.currentScript: The sentence about Mr Darcy starts at line 39. He danced once with Mrs Hurst and once with Miss Bingley. That is two dances, and every dance belongs to Mr Bingley.
rows.whyRewrite: Final clause 'every dance belongs to Mr Bingley' reads literally as false or confusing (Darcy danced two). It means the 'every dance' option describes Mr Bingley; say so plainly, e.g. 'danced every dance' at line 37 is about Mr Bingley.

rows.currentScript: Look at lines 29 to 31. John says they cannot go over the tree or round it. So they turn back to the four crossways. That adds a good six miles to the way home.
rows.whyRewrite: 'That adds a good six miles to the way home' is not what line 30 says. The text says it 'will be a good six miles before we get round to the wooden bridge again', i.e. the detour round to the bridge is six miles, not six miles added to the journey home.

rows.currentScript: Look at lines 13 and 14. Jim is sent round to Mr Goggles. He carries kind regards and a question about the leg. Then comes the errand: will he lend his spirit-level.
rows.whyRewrite: 'He carries kind regards and a question about the leg' misdescribes line 13: 'hopes his leg's better' is a hope, not a question, and the only question is the spirit-level. It also does not show whose leg, which is what the attribute-transfer option turns on.

rows.currentScript: Look at lines 40 and 41. Ilya says there is another cupboard in the annexe. He says Miss said they can do that one on Monday. What he likes about it is getting out of spellings.
rows.whyRewrite: 'What he likes about it is getting out of spellings' claims a feeling the passage does not state, and splits 'get out of spellings' off from Miss's words when line 41 has it inside the same reported sentence ('Miss said we can do that one on Monday and get out of spellings').

rows.currentScript: Go to line 9 and find the word under. It tells you what they stand beneath. Line 10 then splits the job between them. It also says how they found it: splashy, and interesting all the same.
rows.whyRewrite: 'It tells you what they stand beneath' claims something line 9 does not say: they 'washed ... under the spout', nothing about standing. Also 'find the word under' is unquoted, so a child can read it as an instruction to look underneath; quote it ('under').

rows.currentScript: Start at line 21 and find the two things they borrow. One is for the salt, and the other is to put bread on. Read which object does which job. Line 23 adds a joke: they may not have any bread.
rows.whyRewrite: 'find the two things they borrow' is false: the ash-tray and baking-tin are their own things used in place of the right ones (lines 21-22), not borrowed from anyone.

rows.currentScript: Go to line 20 and find the word below. What follows it is the answer. Read on to line 21 and notice further along, which moves you somewhere else. The posts are that somewhere else.
rows.whyRewrite: 'Go to line 20 and find the word below' and 'notice further along' leave the cited words unquoted, so 'find the word below' reads as an instruction to look below the line. Quote them ('Below', 'further along'); content is otherwise correct.
